errors.english: Similarly, on the second and third days, it moves through the joints of the feet
errors.why: The Tibetan assigns the second and third days to the second and third joints of the toe; the following list (foot joint, knee, waist ... crown) goes on day by day, not all on days two and three.

note: A serviceable rendering of a Cakrasaṃvara commentary passage; the lunar-day progression of the bodhicitta is compressed but the ritual sense is intact.

errors.english: the rest of the three bodies—are found through meditating on them as inseparable from the true nature of reality
errors.why: The wisdoms (mirror-like etc.) are obtained by meditating on the three bodies as by nature indivisible; the English folds the three bodies into the list of wisdoms and makes them inseparable 'from' dharmatā.
rgyud phyi ma is the Uttaratantra (the 'Later Tantra'), not an explanatory tantra (bshad rgyud), as the translator's own note half-recognises.

errors.english:
Their abiding state is fourfold:
1. Emanation
2. Collection
errors.why: The opponents' view is given in verse, which the English turns into prose and a numbered list; bsdu ba here is the withdrawal/reabsorption paired with emanation, not 'collection'.

note: The Guhyasamāja vajra-recitation discussion is followable, but several syntactic links are loosened and the opponents' verse is flattened into prose.

errors.english: The master should walk, circling to the right of the student.
errors.why: slob dpon slob ma'i gyas su bskor reads most naturally as master and disciple both moving clockwise (to the right) while striking the lines, not the master circling around the student.

errors.english: Then, the area for the lattices and half-lattices is determined by the measurement of the threshold and the offering plinth.
errors.why: The Tibetan is a chain: the offering ledge takes the measure of the threshold, and the lattice/half-lattice band takes the measure of the offering ledge; the English merges the two steps.

note: A clear rendering of the mandala line-snapping and proportions; the parenthetical glosses on the directional guardians obscure that they name compass directions.

errors.english: Just as a non-returning Bodhisattva reaches the level of non-returning
errors.why: phyir mi ldog pa is avaivartika, 'irreversible'; 'non-returner' is the śrāvaka anāgāmin (phyir mi 'ong ba), a different technical term, and the English uses it throughout the side.

fix.find: Just as a non-returning Bodhisattva reaches the level of non-returning
fix.replace: Just as an irreversible bodhisattva reaches the irreversible stage

errors.english: Although they have attained the eighth stage and have become thoroughly familiar with it in that way
errors.why: The Tibetan compares them to one who has attained the eighth stage ('like one who has attained the eighth stage'); it does not say they have attained it, which makes the following denial of the 'stage of thinning' incoherent.

note: The six vows and the prediction test are rendered well, but the irreversibility passage is mistermed and its comparison misconstrued.

errors.english: You are indeed all the Buddhas, and I am all the Bodhisattvas themselves.
errors.why: The verse says 'I am all the buddhas, all the bodhisattvas'; there is no 'you', and the point (worship one's own self) depends on the first person throughout.

fix.find: You are indeed all the Buddhas, and I am all the Bodhisattvas themselves.
fix.replace: I am indeed all the Buddhas, all the Bodhisattvas themselves.

errors.english: Through the profound devotion of the Great Holder
errors.why: It is the completion-stage yogis' firm conviction (adhimokṣa) of being the great Vajradhara, not Vajradhara's own devotion.

errors.english: a single portion of the supreme activity
errors.why: las kyi rgyal mchog is the named samādhi Karmarājāgrī ('Supreme King of Action'), the third of the three samādhis alongside ādiyoga and maṇḍalarājāgrī, not generic 'supreme activity'.

errors.english: [note: referring to the stabilization of vital essences]
errors.why: The phrase is about drawing out (emitting) the fluid from the samaya, not stabilizing it.

note: The Guhyasamāja commentary is broadly followed, but a reversed person in a quoted verse and a misplaced agent at the start mislead on the self-identification theme.

errors.english: Who are turning the wheel in various ways.
errors.why: The stanza continues 'may I, through the power of my intelligence, also enter their inexhaustible melodious speech', which the English drops.

fix.find: Who are turning the wheel in various ways.
fix.replace:
Who are turning the wheel in various ways—
May I, through the power of my intelligence,
Also enter their inexhaustible melodious speech.

note: A faithful Bhadracarī rendering apart from the dropped half-stanza at the top of the side.
The inference against self-made suffering and its members (dharmin, sādhya, hetu, dṛṣṭānta) are rendered accurately; only small additions like 'purely' and 'exist' in the verse.
An accurate and idiomatic rendering of the degenerations of eon, lifespan and views.

errors.english: One should train in accordance with the nature of reality.
errors.why: Continuing the previous line ('which brings happiness at the beginning and end'), chos nyid here is 'that very dharma' (the meritorious practice, Pali puññam eva), not dharmatā.

note: The sūtra on the five gifts of a good person and their ripening is translated accurately; only the closing verse's opening term is misread.

errors.english: It was for this purpose that I was earnestly sought after by that brahmin
errors.why: Tibetan and Sanskrit (tvaṃ prayatnena yācitā) say that YOU (the girl) were earnestly sought in marriage by that brahmin for my sake.

fix.find: It was for this purpose that I was earnestly sought after by that brahmin
fix.replace: It was for my sake that you were earnestly sought by that brahmin

errors.english: Kapila [note: the father of the bride], who possessed boundless and increasing wealth, having examined the matter,
errors.why: Kapila examined HIM, the suitor of boundless and growing wealth (Skt. tam anantadhanodayam, accusative); the wealth is the groom's, not Kapila's.

fix.find: Kapila [note: the father of the bride], who possessed boundless and increasing wealth, having examined the matter,
fix.replace: Kapila [note: the father of the bride], having examined him, whose wealth was boundless and growing,

note: A fluent rendering of the Pippalāyana-Bhadrā story whose two referent slips are easily corrected against the facing Sanskrit.
